claims.claim: In all five common AttackAir IASA expansions, the delayed pickup timer-write path cannot execute under ordinary sequential C execution.
claims.proof: Reaching ftCo_800D705C requires the preceding local checkItemThrowInput to return false. That false path establishes no pressed A and performs no write; its sole possible helper ftCo_800DF478 is read-only. The next predicate requires pressed A, so it returns false without setting x209C. Earlier callee effects do not invalidate this implication because the false-path read occurs afterward.

claims.claim: Immediate aerial pickup acceptance does not mean a required new fighter motion.
claims.proof: ftCo_800D7100 searches mode1 and calls fn_800D6F58, which assigns and attaches the item, calls owned fttpickupitem_8009447C, and marks pickup state. The owned handler can request recovery/status or consumption and return false; Warp Star/Hammer return true after dedicated entry. The aerial acquisition wrapper ignores that return and reports item acquisition true regardless.

claims.claim: Grounded pickup entry acceptance does mean LightGet/HeavyGet initialization was invoked, but does not reserve the candidate or guarantee later acquisition.
claims.proof: Owned 80094790 calls 80094694 then returns true. Anim later consumes bit3 and repeats a weight-filtered search; a missing or changed candidate is possible.

evidence.why: Aerial attack checker immediately precedes delayed pickup.
False path requires A absent and no C-stick crossing; no mutation on false path.
Delayed predicate requires A and only then writes timer.
Immediate acquisition calls owned notification and immediate-effect helper.
Only Warp Star and Hammer return true from immediate-effect dispatcher.
